title: Murine Hind Limb Explant Model for Studying the Mechanobiology of Achilles Tendon Impingement
protocol: Prepare tissue culture media using Dulbecco's Modified Eagle Medium (1x DMEM) with 1% v/v penicillin-streptomycin.
Add 200 µM L-ascorbic acid to the culture media.
Culture all explants in an incubator at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Supplement the initial 48 h pretreatment culture media with 100 nM dexamethasone.
Change culture media every 48-72 hours for the subsequent 7 days without adding dexamethasone.
Do not add serum, such as fetal bovine serum, to the culture media during the experiment.
Culture explants from the unloaded group in 70 mL of standard culture media.
Prepare approximately 125 mL of culture media for each platform used for baseline tension and static impingement groups.
Euthanize mice via CO2 inhalation and secondary cervical dislocation, or according to institutional guidelines.
Transfer 70 mL of prewarmed (37 °C) culture media into a 100 mm x 25 mm Petri dish in a sterile biological safety cabinet.
Assemble surgical tools including smooth, straight, fine tip forceps; straight, fine tip forceps with serrated teeth; and straight, sharp, fine scissors.
Place the mouse in a supine position and identify the hip joint.
Make a small (5-10 mm) incision through the skin overlaying the proximal and anterior aspect of the upper leg using fine scissors.
Pull the incision apart to expand.
Pinch the exposed upper leg with fingers and carefully pull the skin distally to deglove the hind limb to the level of the ankle.
Gently insert one scissor blade under the skin along the dorsal aspect of the foot and make an incision extending to the toes.
Continue to pull the skin distally to completely remove.
Position the mouse to visualize the Achilles tendon insertion onto the posterior aspect of the calcaneus.
Insert one tip of the smooth, fine-tip forceps between the Achilles tendon and plantaris tendon medially.
Extend the forceps tip proximally under the plantaris tendon.
Tear through the plantaris muscle with the forceps.
Grab the detached proximal end of the plantaris tendon using fine-tip serrated forceps.
Pull distally to remove the plantaris tendon completely.
Use fine scissors to cut through the pelvis at the hip joint and isolate the hind limb.
Pry off the remaining pelvis to expose the femoral head.
Transfer the hind limb explant to a Biological Safety Cabinet (BSC).
Place the hind limb into a dish containing cell culture media with dexamethasone.
Move the dish into an incubator for pretreatment for 48 hours.
Aspirate pretreatment media from explants.
Transfer explants to fresh Petri dishes.
Add 70 mL of culture media to each Petri dish.
Return explant plates to the incubator.
Cut pieces of sandpaper similar in size to grip platens for baseline tension and static impingement groups.
Cut pieces of braided line approximately 18 inches in length and pre-tie a loose overhand knot halfway along the length for the static impingement group.
Tear pieces of aluminum foil to cover each acrylic bath.
Spray pieces of aluminum foil with 70% ethanol (EtOH).
Transfer all preparations to the Biological Safety Cabinet (BSC).
Place an acrylic bath, base, volume reduction insert, clip, and grips in secondary containers for leak protection.
Submerge components in ≥ 10% bleach solution and soak for at least 1 hour.
Rinse off bleach solution with tap water.
Autoclave all tap water or use purified water as needed for contamination control.
Attach platens to the grips using M3 screws and compression springs.
Secure the grips to the base using an M5 screw.
Insert M6 screws until they engage the platens.
Attach sandpaper to the platens with double-sided tape.
Close the grips to promote adhesion of the sandpaper.
Place the upper leg and knee between the platens with the superficial surface of the Achilles tendon facing upward when ready to load a platform.
Loosely close the grips to gently hold the leg in place.
Grab the exposed femoral head or foot using forceps.
Manipulate the knee flexion angle as you gradually close the grips to secure it in place.
Extend the knee joint for the baseline tension group as described previously.
Flex the knee joint between the grips for the static impingement group.
Place the overhand knot of the string around the distal paw and tighten.
Route the string through a slot in the base located underneath the explant and through the clip hole.
Place the base into the acrylic bath and secure the clip to the top edge of the bath.
Pull the string to dorsiflex the foot to at least 110° with respect to the tibia.
Mark the string as it exits the clip using a permanent marker.
Take a photograph of the explant in this position for later quantification of dorsiflexion angle.
Remove the base and attach the volume reduction insert by sliding along a track on the base.
Place the base (now attached to the volume reduction insert) back into the acrylic bath and reposition the clip on the top edge.
Pull the string to return to the original dorsiflexion angle using the marked string as a guide.
Secure the string to the outside of the bath with tape to maintain static dorsiflexion.
Place the base with volume reduction insert into the acrylic bath once the explant is positioned between the grips for the baseline tension group.
Take a photograph of the explant in this position for quantification of dorsiflexion angle.
Add 125 ml of prewarmed (37 °C) culture media to each platform to submerge explants.
Cover the top of the bath with aluminum foil, place in a secondary container, and move into the incubator.
Culture for 7 additional days, changing media every 48-72 h.
Trim toenails/distal toes and cut away the upper leg proximal to the Achilles myotendinous junction.
Place each trimmed ankle joint into a processing cassette lined with foam biopsy pads.
Push the ankle into the cassette corner to position the ankle at approximately 90° dorsiflexion.
Close the cassette to keep in place.
Fix for 3 days in 10% neutral buffered formalin (NBF).
Decalcify for 2 weeks in 14% ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA) dissolved in distilled water (diH₂O), with pH adjusted to 7.4-7.6 with glacial acetic acid.
Rinse samples three times each in both 1x phosphate buffered saline (PBS) and diH₂O for 5 minutes each.
Dehydrate through a graded series of EtOH.
Clear in xylene.
Infiltrate with paraffin wax.
Trim into the sample until sections are parallel to the block face.
Grossly trim into the ankle from the medial aspect of the joint, stopping before reaching the medial border of the Achilles tendon insertion.
Transfer the sample to an ice block to adjust temperature and hydration.
Change blades or shift to a fresh section of the current blade.
Continue sectioning into the sample at 10 µm thickness.
Carefully identify entry into the Achilles tendon insertion with a brightfield microscope.
Perform serial sectioning tracking section number through the entire Achilles tendon insertion.
Select level-matched tissue sections from each pair of contralateral limbs for each assay.
Place selected sections on a slide rack.
Move slides through 3 changes of xylene, 2 changes of 100% EtOH, and 2 changes of 95% EtOH.
Change to 1 change of 70% EtOH.
Finish rehydrating in diH2O.
Incubate sections in 20 µg/mL proteinase K for 20 min at room temperature.
Rinse sections in diH2O after proteinase K treatment.
Incubate in 50 µL of TUNEL stain solution (5 µL enzyme solution, 45 µL label solution) for 1 h at 37 °C.
Rinse sections in diH2O after incubation.
Mount sections with antifade reagent containing DAPI and coverslip.
Image the Achilles tendon insertion using a fluorescence microscope with a 4x objective lens.
Include a DAPI channel to visualize all nuclei (excitation/emission wavelengths = 360/460 nm).
Visualize apoptotic nuclei through a TUNEL (TMR Red) channel (excitation/emission wavelengths = 540/580 nm).
If possible, include a brightfield channel for imaging.
Import images into an image analysis software suitable for ROI-based processing.
Define a region of interest outlining the entire Achilles tendon in view, excluding cells in the epitenon.
Perform ROI selection in MATLAB by importing the brightfield image.
Use the drawpolygon() function to trace and enclose the boundaries of the tendon.
Create a Polygon object for the ROI using MATLAB.
Apply the ROI mask to DAPI and TUNEL channel images using createMask().
Identify a fluorescence intensity threshold for defining apoptotic nuclei.
Normalize the fluorescence intensity threshold to the maximum fluorescence intensity of apoptotic nuclei in nonviable tissues.
Calculate the fraction of apoptotic nuclei (TUNEL+ nuclei/DAPI nuclei) within the Achilles tendon.

Transfer slide rack with level-matched tissue sections from contralateral pairs of explants to 0.4% w/v Toluidine blue O in 0.1 M sodium acetate buffer with pH adjusted to 4.0 using glacial acetic acid.
Incubate for 10 min at room temperature.
Rinse 3x in diH2O for 30 s each.
Dehydrate through three changes of 95% EtOH and two changes of 100% EtOH, 30 s each.
Clear through three changes of xylene, 1 min each.
Coverslip with xylene-based mounting medium.
Obtain 24-bit Red-Blue-Green (RGB) color images of the Achilles tendon insertion.
Import RGB images into an image analysis software capable of defining and managing multiple ROIs.
Set the pixel/length scale.
Identify the intersection of the deep tendon border with the calcaneus in the image displayed in the software.
Trace proximally 800 µm along the deep tendon border to establish the deep boundary of the CTF.
Draw a line segment connecting from the established deep boundary position to the superficial tendon border, perpendicular to the local fiber orientation.
Define the distal boundary of the CTF by drawing a line segment connecting from the intersection point to the superficial tendon border along the distinct tidemark separating the CTF and AZF.
Generate the superficial boundary of the CTF by tracing the superficial tendon border to enclose.
Divide the total CTF into 4 quadrants.
Connect the midpoint of the deep and superficial CTF boundaries with a line segment to create a distal/proximal boundary.
Pass through the midpoint of the distal/proximal boundary, connect the midpoints of the distal and proximal CTF boundaries along the fiber orientation to create a superficial/deep boundary.
Compile vertices defining the boundaries of each individual ROI (CTF, quadrants 1-4) into vectors in MATLAB.
Generate enclosed Polygon objects for each ROI using images.roi.Polygon() in MATLAB.
Transform RGB pixel data into the Hue-Saturation-Value (HSV) color space using the color transformer plugin in FIJI or rgb2hsv() function in MATLAB.
Project HSV data into the 2D hue-saturation space to encode unique colors for each combination of hue and saturation.
Calculate the average hue and saturation within each ROI that describe the average stain color in the ROI.
Analyze hue-saturation pixel data specifically within each ROI using createMask() with Polygon objects defining each ROI.
Define a small ROI within the periosteal fibrocartilage (PF).
Calculate the average hue and saturation for the defined ROI.
Calculate the Euclidean distance separating the average color of each ROI in the calcified tissue from that of the PF.
Use the calculated distances to determine the fibrocartilage score, ranging from -1 to 1 based on color similarity to PF.
Average data for hue, saturation, and fibrocartilage score within each ROI across multiple tissue sections.
Perform paired statistical comparisons between groups of contralateral limbs.
Perform SHG imaging of Toluidine blue-stained sections using a microscope system with a 20x objective lens.
Acquire z-stacks through the section thickness for detailed analysis.
Perform tile scanning if necessary to fully capture the Achilles tendon insertion area.
Import SHG images into a preferred image analysis software.
Define ROIs encompassing and subdividing the CTF at the Achilles tendon insertion as described for Toluidine blue image analysis in section 8.
If SHG images are imported into MATLAB, use the approach for defining CTF ROIs in MATLAB as outlined in section 8.
Export ROI vertices from MATLAB as .txt files after defining ROIs.
Import ROI coordinates into FIJI using File > Import > XY Coordinates.
Overlay the selection and send to the ROI manager for analysis in FIJI.
Use the Directionality plugin in FIJI to quantify collagen organization.
Perform Fourier spectrum analysis to calculate distributions of fiber orientations across small windows spanning a ROI.
Calculate the dispersion, which is inversely related to fiber alignment.
Import SHG images into FIJI.
Set the pixel/length scale in FIJI.
Project maximum pixel intensity data into a 2D composite image.
Add ROIs to the ROI Manager.
Sequentially overlay each CTF ROI onto the image.
Draw 10 small sub-ROIs of consistent size within the ROI.
Add the sub-ROIs to the ROI manager.
Within each sub-ROI, run the directionality plugin in FIJI to calculate fiber dispersion.
Average dispersion data across sub-ROIs within each CTF ROI.
Average dispersion data within each CTF ROI across sections from each explant.
Perform paired statistical comparisons between groups of contralateral limbs.
